first_impression.reaction: My assistant opened it, not me. The first screen is calm and not salesy, so it didn't get closed straight away. Nobody says 'affordable', nobody is shouting. But it reads like a blog post for any couple with a lawn. My assistant's summary would be: tasteful, a useful checklist, nothing that shows they work at our scale or handle privacy. She skimmed the real weddings and the venue questions and skipped most of the styling.

journey.quote: It works when the styling and the backup plan are decided together, because the garden that sets the mood is also the venue with the least shelter from the weather.
journey.reaction: Sensible and quietly said. That's the tone I want from a planner. No gushing.

journey.quote: In Dubai, [Rasha and Mahmoud](/a-vibrant-garden-wedding-in-dubai) split their wedding between an indoor space and an outdoor one.
journey.reaction: The only story that feels close to home. Splitting indoor and outdoor matters for a Dubai wedding. It's just two lines though, and says nothing about how big it was or how it was run.

journey.quote: [Helen and Trent](/helen-and-trents-intimate-garden-wedding) exchanged vows on her family's private estate in Victoria.
journey.reaction: A family estate is relevant to us. But 'intimate' and 'styled themselves' tells me this was small and DIY. Most of these stories are about fairy lights and handmade arches, not hundreds of guests.

journey.quote: One long table under trees turns dinner into a single conversation, and two or three parallel runs do the same for a larger guest list.
journey.reaction: Two or three runs is a big dinner for most people. For 300 guests it's not even a start. This is the clearest sign the article isn't written with a guest list like ours in mind.

journey.quote: Mismatched china, printed linen and flowers that look picked rather than arranged all read as garden party.
journey.reaction: Charming for someone else. Not our family's look. My assistant would skip this.

journey.quote: Sunscreen goes on at least 20 minutes before going outside and again every two hours, so set a sunscreen station out well before guests take their seats.
journey.reaction: Over-explained. I don't need to be told when to apply sunscreen. It makes the piece feel like it's written for a first-timer doing it all herself.

journey.section: What to plan for with your venue
journey.quote: Each point below ends in questions to ask before you book, and the answers belong in writing.
journey.reaction: Good. Getting things in writing is how I'd want it handled. The question lists are practical and my assistant would keep them.

journey.quote: Which areas are closed to guests, and can vehicles drive onto the lawn for set up?
journey.reaction: This is the one place it nearly asks my question, but backwards. I don't care which areas are closed to my guests. I care whether the whole place can be closed to everyone else.

journey.quote: How do guests travel between the hotel and the garden, and how long does it take?
journey.reaction: Fair question, but for us it's private transfers, arrival times for VIPs and our security. Nothing here about exclusive use, security or privacy, which is what decides whether I call anyone.

journey.quote: Through [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=garden-wedding&utm_content=secondary), a Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Working in my time zone is useful with family in Dubai, Sydney and London. 'Confirms inclusions' sounds like a package, though. I don't want inclusions, I want to know what's possible.

journey.section: Plan your garden wedding with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: One Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world as your single point of contact from start to finish, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: One point of contact who handles everything, anywhere, is the right promise. Said plainly, without discount talk. It still doesn't tell me they've done a wedding our size.

unanswered_questions: Has Wedded Concierge planned a wedding of 200 to 400 guests, and can they show one privately?
Can they arrange exclusive use of a garden venue for several days, closed to the public?
How do they work with a family's own security team and the venue's?
Do they arrange private transfers and VIP arrivals for guests flying in from several countries?
What do they do to keep a wedding out of the press and off social media (guest phone policies, NDAs with vendors, photo approval before anything is published)?
Can they handle halal catering and family customs for a Dubai or Middle Eastern family?
Is there a private channel or a named senior person to speak to, rather than a general enquiry form?

turn_offs_found.quote: Sunscreen goes on at least 20 minutes before going outside and again every two hours, so set a sunscreen station out well before guests take their seats.
turn_offs_found.why: Over-explaining. It reads as advice for a couple doing it themselves, not for a client with a full team.

turn_offs_found.quote: a Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
turn_offs_found.why: 'Inclusions' is package language. It makes me feel like a standard package client.

would_share_with: My assistant would keep the venue question lists for the planner we hire. I wouldn't send the article to family.

cta_reaction.quote: Tell [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=garden-wedding&utm_content=closing) the garden you have in mind, your month and how many guests are coming.
cta_reaction.why: The ask is simple and not pushy, which I like. But I don't enquire through a blog link. My assistant might click to see who's behind it. If nothing there shows large weddings handled discreetly and a private way to talk, we'd wait for a referral instead.

top_3_changes:
In 'Garden protection rules', add an exclusive-use question. OLD: "- Which areas are closed to guests, and can vehicles drive onto the lawn for set up?" NEW: "- Which areas are closed to guests, and can vehicles drive onto the lawn for set up?
- Can the gardens be closed to the public and to other guests for the whole event?"

In 'Destination garden weddings', add a security and transfers question. OLD: "- Who is on the venue's side on the day, and do they stay until the end of the night?" NEW: "- Who is on the venue's side on the day, and do they stay until the end of the night?
- Can a family's own security team work alongside the venue's, and can guests be met with private transfers?"

In the closing CTA, invite privacy needs without promising anything. OLD: "the garden you have in mind, your month and how many guests are coming." NEW: "the garden you have in mind, your month, how many guests are coming and anything about the day that needs to stay private."

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction quotes an exact sentence from the draft
Stayed in character as Layla (UHNW, assistant reads first, understated, privacy and scale first)
No invented brand facts; capability gaps listed as unanswered questions
HTML comments, image slots and LINK markers treated as invisible
Suggested edits are exact old/new strings that add no prices, venue or vendor names, statistics, business details or new facts about the real weddings
Scores are 1 to 5 for all five required fields

assumptions: Persona card is provisional and not CRM-calibrated, so reactions reflect the assumed profile.
Read as Layla's assistant skimming first, then Layla glancing at the summary and the sections the assistant flagged.
A broad 'garden wedding ideas' post is not expected to be written mainly for UHNW readers; low relevance is reported as honest fit, not a defect of the article.

open_questions.question: Should a broad inspiration post carry any scale or discretion signals for UHNW readers, or is that left to Concierge landing pages? The suggested edits are questions only and add no service claims.
Does the brand want to keep 'confirms inclusions in writing'? For this persona 'inclusions' reads as package language.
